E2.evidence: Step 1: the image_geometry Python library (vision_opencv) and the numpy library, separately released. Step 2: the effect depends on the provider revision: numpy's matrix.__new__ gained `warnings.warn('the matrix subclass is not the recommended way to ' ... PendingDeprecationWarning, stacklevel=2)` at v1.15.0 (absent at v1.14.6), so image_geometry's unchanged `numpy.matrix(L, dtype='float64')` warns only with newer numpy. Steps 3-5: the resolving change rewrites image_geometry's use of the numpy API; not wiring, build, or firmware.

E3.evidence: UPGRADE: image_geometry still constructs numpy.matrix as it could without warning before numpy's pending deprecation, while running against a numpy that deprecates the subclass.

units.name: image_geometry
units.revision_basis: Issue #524 (2024-03-23) links cameramodels.py at 8b42d66f4946f4204387b30aabc8c2921e5d9f47, which was also the rolling head on that date. The fix is PR #527 (merge 25b733e27ab11e6e92fd217152d77a86ac91c3c1, 2024-04-18); the reporter names the release carrying it ("the updated image_geometry 4.1.0 package"), and tag 4.1.0 (f5b738d9694f0cee5904440d03912fc249943f8a) contains the merge.

units.name: numpy
units.revision_basis: The numpy version is not stated. Bounds: the quoted warning text is emitted by numpy/matrixlib/defmatrix.py from v1.15.0 on (checked identical at v1.15.0, v1.21.5, v2.0.0; absent at v1.14.6), so the provider is at or after v1.15.0. The reporter's test run in PR #526 shows "platform linux -- Python 3.10.12", the Ubuntu 22.04 Python used by rolling at the time; v1.21.5 (Ubuntu 22.04's python3-numpy) is inferred on that basis and could differ for a pip-installed numpy. image_geometry's package.xml at the broken revision declares no numpy dependency. The resolution does not change numpy.

failed_conditions.quote: image_geometry/cameramodels.py uses deprecated `numpy.matrix` subclass causing runtime `PendingDeprecationWarning`.

loudness_evidence: numpy's own deprecation diagnostic, shown in the PR #526 test run: "Warning: the matrix subclass is not the recommended way to represent matrices or deal with linear algebra (see https://docs.scipy.org/doc/numpy/user/numpy-for-matlab-users.html). Please adjust your code to use regular ndarray." (https://github.com/ros-perception/vision_opencv/pull/526). It is raised at run time when the matrix is constructed (issue #524: "This will cause the warning during initialization every time the public API members below are called").

resolution.summary: image_geometry stops constructing numpy.matrix in its supported API: mkmat builds numpy.ndarray (np.array), new snake_case methods return ndarray, and the old camelCase methods and K/D/R/P/full_K/full_P properties are kept as @deprecated wrappers that still return numpy.matrix (PR #527, released in image_geometry 4.1.0).
resolution.evidence: The contributor reports the warning gone after the fix ("The original issue has been fixed with https://github.com/ros-perception/vision_opencv/pull/527." on image_pipeline #572, with a camera_calibration test log that no longer lists the matrix warning), but the numpy revision of that run is not given.

notes: Class element_retyped is used for a deprecation: numpy.matrix's declaration changed (its constructor now warns) while the element is still present. consumer_built_against.broken v1.14.6 is the last numpy tag before the warning was added (inferred from the consumer's unconditional use of numpy.matrix); consumer_built_against.resolved is the provider revision the fixed consumer ran against (same inference as numpy's broken_rev). The deprecated wrappers kept in 4.1.0 still call numpy.matrix, so callers of the deprecated API still get numpy's warning. Other compositions touched by these sources: (1) downstream image_pipeline camera_calibration tests, where the warning was first seen (image_pipeline #572, on foxy) and which after the fix get image_geometry's own deprecation warnings ("Call to deprecated method fromCameraInfo. ..."); (2) PR #526 fixed image_geometry's directed.py test, which used ROS 1 CameraInfo field names against ROS 2 sensor_msgs ("AttributeError: 'CameraInfo' object has no attribute 'D'") and had been disabled since the ROS 2 port.
